     9	
    10	# Common Practice foundation review
    11	
    12	Use Common Practice's application structure and ordinary development workflow.
    13	Prioritise the Cloudflare Website and API, remove every Alchemy patch, and remove
    14	TaxKit's separate receipt and approval machinery. Keep Bun as a supported,
    15	secondary host over the same calculation packages.
    16	
    17	```text
    18	Website server/browser -> checked RPC operations -> API -> calculations -> rules/core
    19	Machine HTTP/RPC/MCP -----------------------------> API -> calculations -> rules/core
    20	Local SDK ----------------------------------------------> calculations -> rules/core
    21	
    22	Checked stage settings -> API declaration -> Website declaration
    23	                                      API address + private binding -> Website
    24	Git commit/PR -> ordinary checks -> native Alchemy -> deployed Website/API
    25	                               Doppler supplies stage-specific secrets
    26	```
    27	
    28	The comparison uses TaxKit commit `f899c963f463d2283517e908febcfa3ebb1dd442`,
    29	Common Practice commit `54a62a5d64892ee2304260f51ef683fb299deea7`, and Commonplace
    30	`development-workflows` 0.6.11, checked against its published release on
    31	10 October 2026. This document and its [plan](../exec-plans/active/common-practice-foundation-review.md)
    32	replace the large, uncommitted audit packet created during this review.
    33	
    34	This remains the agreed research and design stage. Application code, dependency
    35	versions, hosted workflows, provider resources and credentials have not changed.
    36	The latest instructions determine the proposed direction; they do not require a
    37	new JSON acceptance record for each finding. Common Practice is read-only.
    38	
    39	## Agreed direction
    40	
    41	| Choice | Direction |
    42	| --- | --- |
    43	| Website calls | Keep the current typed RPC calls for this change; adopt Common Practice's checked client and application ownership. Improve the HTTP client separately. |
    44	| Hosts | Cloudflare first. Keep Bun and Cloudflare, with shared packages independent of either. Preserve Bun's current HTTP coverage; adding RPC/MCP to Bun is outside this change. |
    45	| Alchemy | Zero Alchemy patches, including replacement monkeypatches, copied planner code or a custom provider carrying the same fixes. Redesign the declarations that currently need them. |
    46	| Development and operations | Ordinary commits, pull requests, checks, GitHub Actions, native Alchemy and native Doppler, following Common Practice. Remove receipt packets, duplicated approval records and checks whose only purpose is to verify that paperwork. |
    47	| Operational information | Allow fixed safe details such as app, stage, route category, duration and safe failure category. Exclude salaries, facts, results, calculation traces, raw URLs, request bodies and raw errors. PostHog remains postponed. |
    48	
    49	The host and privacy choices are also recorded in [ADR 0003](../adr/0003-support-independent-api-hosts.md)
    50	and [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-limit-operational-observations.md). The earlier
    51	[shared Axiom dataset choice](../adr/0002-reuse-shared-telemetry-datasets.md)
    52	remains: reference the existing three physical datasets, with TaxKit-owned scoped
    53	access and destinations. No collection is enabled by this review.
    54	
    55	## What to copy from Common Practice
    56	
    57	| Area | Common Practice source | TaxKit adoption |
    58	| --- | --- | --- |
    59	| Server execution | `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts` | One frontend server runtime, constructed in the application. Services and tax packages never start their own runtime. |
    60	| Browser state | `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts` | One React-mounted Atom state graph. Keep TaxKit's existing form commands and cancellation. |
    61	| Checked clients | `packages/http/src/client.layer.ts`, `packages/rpc/src/client.layer.ts`, `packages/content/src/service.ts` | Keep generated clients private; expose named operations through a checked service, with live and test implementations. |
    62	| Private Cloudflare calls | `apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts` | Put Cloudflare binding conversion in one Website-owned adapter. Use native Alchemy conversion where it preserves caller trust and complete reply handling. |
    63	| Resource declarations | `alchemy.run.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/build/cloudflare.ts`, `apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts` | Declare the API before the Website. Website uses the API's actual address and private binding. Keep deployment code at the app/infrastructure owners. |
    64	| Secrets | `packages/infrastructure/src/secrets.ts` | One native source list: Doppler, ignored `.env` overrides, disabled shell-value fallback. Keep TaxKit's own project, configs and credentials. |
    65	| Commands | Root `package.json` | Short commands calling native Alchemy directly. Keep one understandable verification command. |
    66	| Automation | `.github/workflows/checks.yml`, `preview.yml`, `production.yml` | Checks on PR/main; PR previews and close-event cleanup; manual main-only Production. Native dry-run/deploy, small public smoke checks and native Production drift. |
    67	| Everyday records | Git commits, PRs, workflow logs and Alchemy state | Use these ordinary records. No additional repository receipt files or approval-envelope system. |
    68	
    69	These are paths within Common Practice, not personal checkout paths. Reuse the
    70	approach and required code, not its project names, access tokens or provider IDs.
    71	
    72	Common Practice still runs build, formatting, lint, types, Effect checks, tests,
    73	unused-code and documentation checks. Its workflow does not support a claim that
    74	all verification disappears. TaxKit should remove checks of ceremony while
    75	keeping tests that catch wrong tax answers, broken public contracts or a broken
    76	Website/API.
    77	
    78	## Complete calls and the HTTP/RPC comparison
    79	
    80	A host is the environment running the API, such as Cloudflare or Bun. HTTP, RPC
    81	and MCP are different ways to send a request to that same API. The local SDK is
    82	a library that calculates inside the caller's program.
    83	
    84	| Call | Current path and behaviour to preserve |
    85	| --- | --- |
    86	| Browser calculation | Page container -> Atom command -> checked public RPC address -> API handler -> `PublicCalculatorService` -> catalogue/fact checks -> Australian rules/Core -> checked report -> the same Atom state and rendering leaf. Editing or leaving the page cancels pending browser work. |
    87	| Server HTML form | Website checks the 64 KiB POST -> server service -> private API method carrying the checked original caller identity separately from JSON -> the same calculation service -> checked submission data. Keep working without JavaScript. |
    88	| Machine HTTP | HTTP declarations decode requests with the owning Schemas -> handler -> the same calculation service -> existing status/error envelope. The new client adds named checked operations around these declarations. |
    89	| Machine RPC | Revision-four checked operations -> the same service. Keep the current encoded replies and safe named failures. |
    90	| Remote MCP | API tool definitions reuse the owning Schemas and shared service. Keep current request/cancellation ownership and Cloudflare session support. |
    91	| Local SDK | Checked in-process request -> the same calculation service. Effect callers own their services; the Promise-facing SDK privately owns its necessary runtime and closes it. It does not become a network SDK. |
    92	
    93	| Comparison | Common Practice | TaxKit decision |
    94	| --- | --- | --- |
    95	| Website transport | Typed HTTP over a private binding; ordinary page reads use server functions. Its RPC client exists but is not the Website's chosen path. | Keep Website RPC because it already covers calculator and documentation operations. Copy client ownership rather than force an HTTP rewrite. |
    96	| Named services | HTTP and RPC implement its Content service; raw generated clients are private. | RPC already has named checked operations. Add the equivalent HTTP approach, keeping existing exports as compatibility adapters. |
    97	| Error ownership | Remote client errors become safe Content-owned errors. | A remote call can fail differently from a local calculation. Use one owning checked remote-operation contract, with existing RPC names retained; do not pretend transport errors are local engine errors or add another generic facade. |
    98	| Original caller identity | Content reads do not have TaxKit's anonymous-calculation rate policy. | Preserve the private method's trusted caller key. Plain forwarded headers from a binding are insufficient. Interpret Cloudflare edge headers in the host, not the shared RPC package. |
    99	| Cancellation | Native HTTP binding can carry an operation signal. | Browser RPC cancellation stays. The current private RPC method cannot send an AbortSignal remotely: it stops waiting locally; remote work has its five-second budget. Do not claim immediate remote cancellation. |
   100	| Reply limits | Content uses a longer timeout for image rendering. | Keep TaxKit's ten-second complete-reply limit, 2 MiB response cap and no automatic retries. Give the new HTTP client equivalent full-read limits. |
   101	| RPC lifetime | Common Practice acquires its RPC client once. | Keep TaxKit's per-operation client scope: a receive loop left on an earlier Cloudflare request can stall the next request. Copying the once-acquired loop would undo a deliberate fix. |
   102	| Documentation | HTTP has selected content/Markdown/SEO/image operations. | TaxKit also needs discovery, navigation, page, search and Markdown. An HTTP-only Website would need equivalent checked coverage; do not add a second content renderer. |
   103	| Package consumers | Common Practice's packages are private and source-oriented. | Keep TaxKit's compiled exports, actual packed SDK entry points and clean downstream consumer checks when those contracts change. |
   104	
   105	This resolves the Website choice for the foundation change. A later HTTP switch
   106	can be assessed on its own merit; it is not required to adopt Common Practice.
   107	
   108	## Cloudflare first, with host-independent packages
   109	
   110	Use Effect services and Layers to describe shared operations and supply their
   111	implementations. Core, rule, calculator and transport packages must not import
   112	Cloudflare, Alchemy or Bun server code, interpret trusted Cloudflare headers, or
   113	run Effects themselves. The SDK's private Promise adapter is a justified public
   114	library execution boundary.
   115	
   116	The API app owns the host adapters. Cloudflare supplies native request context,
   117	private bindings, rate services and sessions. Bun supplies its HTTP server and
   118	configuration through one top-level runner. Both use the same tax operations.
   119	Do not add a managed Promise runtime to the native API Worker.
   120	
   121	Matching upstream Effect 4.0.2 supports this separation: `HttpApiBuilder` captures
   122	shared services, `HttpRouter` supplies the current request scope, and
   123	`BunHttpServer` supplies the abstract server. `HttpRouter.provideRequest` builds
   124	its supplied Layer per request; it must not own an application-wide capacity
   125	pool. Alchemy's Worker bridge builds the application once and supplies native
   126	request context. Stream cleanup belongs to the current consumer; isolate
   127	shutdown is not a guaranteed cleanup hook.
   128	
   129	Cloudflare already captures one bounded calculation service. Keep its shared
   130	eight-place pool, five-second work budget, exact Website Origin and checked
   131	private identity. A timer cannot interrupt synchronous calculation code.
   132	
   133	Bun currently builds the bounded service per request, creating a fresh pool for
   134	each one. Fix that at Bun application composition after the Cloudflare work.
   135	Keep its current HTTP coverage and explicitly owned CORS/admission differences;
   136	no Cloudflare Durable Object substitute or new Bun protocol promise is needed.
   137	
   138	## Patch-free Alchemy design
   139	
   140	TaxKit currently locks Effect 4.0.0 and patched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.80. Common
   141	Practice locks Effect 4.0.2 and unpatched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.81. The target is the
   142	compatible, published, unpatched upstream package used by Common Practice,
   143	checked against TaxKit's installed types and consumers during implementation.
   144	An upstream comparison is not an installation or a completed upgrade.
   145	
   146	Two declarations need to change before removing the current Alchemy patch:
   147	
   148	1. **Remove the two-way output dependency.** In
   149	   `packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.ts`, Website uses API output/binding
   150	   while API reads Website output. Replace API's reverse dependency with one
   151	   checked, stage-owned exact Website address. The same settings own its domain
   152	   or checked Worker name. For Preview, retain the actual existing Worker name
   153	   and use Alchemy's native checked account-subdomain setting; do not guess the
   154	   generated hostname or add Preview DNS as an incidental change. API retains
   155	   its own `Worker.URL`; Website consumes
   156	   API output and retains its own `Worker.URL`. Declare API, then Website.
   157	   Confirm native local development addresses before implementation: local ports
   158	   can be assigned at runtime. Do not widen allowed Origins to `*` or infer an
   159	   address from arbitrary request headers to solve this.
   160	2. **Avoid the shared redirect write.** Remove `domain.redirects` from the
   161	   Website declaration. Attach the native apex and `www` domain aliases to the
   162	   Website, then return the existing permanent redirect to the canonical apex
   163	   at Website ingress, before routes or calculator forms. Preserve path/query
   164	   semantics and the current redirect status. This bypasses the Worker
   165	   provider's shared-zone redirect ruleset code without a custom provider.
   166	   Common Practice itself uses `domain.redirects`; this field is a necessary
   167	   TaxKit departure. Previously saved redirect declarations can invoke the
   168	   same provider path during removal, so check the existing-state transition
   169	   before calling the migration safe. No patched replacement is permitted.
   170	
   171	Upstream beta.81 still treats every shared redirect-rules read failure as an
   172	absent ruleset. The earlier mocked forbidden-read case produced a replacement
   173	write. That shows a problem with blindly keeping this declaration while deleting
   174	the patch; it does not require retaining the patch. A separate native Ruleset
   175	resource owns an entire zone phase, so it is unsuitable unless TaxKit owns every
   176	rule in that phase. Use the Website alias/redirect approach instead.
   177	
   178	Remove the Alchemy entry from `patchedDependencies`, its patch file, and the
   179	corresponding lockfile patch references together. Search build, install and
   180	infrastructure code for every other Alchemy modification. Do not relocate a fix
   181	into a wrapper, copied source or postinstall step. Preserve logical resource IDs,
   182	stack/state identities and the existing unrelated DNS records.
   183	
   184	The Atom scheduler peer-metadata patch is unrelated to Alchemy. Common Practice
   185	also has non-Alchemy Effect/PostHog patches; those are not required by this
   186	proposal and must not be copied without a TaxKit need. Align the Effect family
   187	and explicit companion override if choosing 4.0.2. Any React/Atom compatibility
   188	change needs ordinary type/build/browser checks, not a new exception receipt.
   189	
   190	## Ordinary commits, deployments and Doppler
   191	
   192	Copy Common Practice's workflow shape:
   193	
   194	- Make normal coherent Git commits and PRs. Describe the change and meaningful
   195	  test results in the PR. Do not require an approval JSON, finding crosswalk,
   196	  source-digest receipt or separate commit acceptance ceremony.
   197	- Run one ordinary check workflow. Use the same verification command locally
   198	  and in Actions, rather than a second release-policy graph that rechecks every
   199	  earlier document and receipt.
   200	- On an internal PR, install the frozen lockfile, check the change, then run
   201	  native Alchemy dry-run and deploy for that PR's stage. Check the Website/API.
   202	  On close, use native destroy restricted to that PR stage. Keep fork secrets
   203	  excluded, same-stage deployment/cleanup serialised, and the current PR-state
   204	  check. These prevent real mistakes and are small enough to understand.
   205	- Production runs manually from `main`: ordinary verification, native dry-run,
   206	  native deploy, native drift, and a small public Website/API check. Use existing
   207	  GitHub environment settings; do not add a second TaxKit approval system.
   208	- Use native `Doppler.Secrets`, `.env` and disabled `ProcessEnv` fallback in one
   209	  owner, following Common Practice. `.env` overrides also apply in hosted runs;
   210	  Actions should write deployment metadata only. Retain TaxKit's actual Doppler
   211	  project/config mapping and environment-scoped read-only Doppler credentials.
   212	  Do not copy another project's values or duplicate Cloudflare keys in GitHub.
   213	- Roll back by redeploying the previous working Git revision through the same
   214	  native workflow. Alchemy resource retention is not a deployment snapshot.
   215	
   216	Target scripts are short native commands such as `dev`, `pr:plan`, `pr:deploy`,
   217	`pr:destroy`, `production:plan`, `production:deploy` and `production:drift`.
   218	The names can match Common Practice while selecting TaxKit's existing `prod`
   219	and `pr-N` state identities. Do not rename a live stack/stage as a side effect
   220	of making commands prettier. Native local development still needs its exact
   221	address and state behaviour checked; delete custom wrappers once their useful
   222	behaviour is covered by the native entrypoint.
   223	
   224	GitHub records the commit and run; Alchemy records state; the smoke check
   225	confirms the deployed endpoints. No separate receipt workflow, deployment
   226	manifest, hash catalogue, custody packet or per-step approval file is needed.
   227	A request to review the design does not itself deploy it, delete resources or
   228	rotate secrets, but those ordinary task boundaries do not need a bespoke record
   229	system. Current Actions credit availability has not been rechecked here.
   230	
   231	## Remove ceremony at its source

   108	## Cloudflare first, with host-independent packages
   109	
   110	Use Effect services and Layers to describe shared operations and supply their
   111	implementations. Core, rule, calculator and transport packages must not import
   112	Cloudflare, Alchemy or Bun server code, interpret trusted Cloudflare headers, or
   113	run Effects themselves. The SDK's private Promise adapter is a justified public
   114	library execution boundary.

   116	The API app owns the host adapters. Cloudflare supplies native request context,
   117	private bindings, rate services and sessions. Bun supplies its HTTP server and
   118	configuration through one top-level runner. Both use the same tax operations.
   119	Do not add a managed Promise runtime to the native API Worker.

   122	shared services, `HttpRouter` supplies the current request scope, and
   123	`BunHttpServer` supplies the abstract server. `HttpRouter.provideRequest` builds
   124	its supplied Layer per request; it must not own an application-wide capacity
   125	pool. Alchemy's Worker bridge builds the application once and supplies native
   126	request context. Stream cleanup belongs to the current consumer; isolate
   127	shutdown is not a guaranteed cleanup hook.

   130	eight-place pool, five-second work budget, exact Website Origin and checked
   131	private identity. A timer cannot interrupt synchronous calculation code.

   134	each one. Fix that at Bun application composition after the Cloudflare work.

    97	| Error ownership | Remote client errors become safe Content-owned errors. | A remote call can fail differently from a local calculation. Use one owning checked remote-operation contract, with existing RPC names retained; do not pretend transport errors are local engine errors or add another generic facade. |
    98	| Original caller identity | Content reads do not have TaxKit's anonymous-calculation rate policy. | Preserve the private method's trusted caller key. Plain forwarded headers from a binding are insufficient. Interpret Cloudflare edge headers in the host, not the shared RPC package. |
    99	| Cancellation | Native HTTP binding can carry an operation signal. | Browser RPC cancellation stays. The current private RPC method cannot send an AbortSignal remotely: it stops waiting locally; remote work has its five-second budget. Do not claim immediate remote cancellation. |
   100	| Reply limits | Content uses a longer timeout for image rendering. | Keep TaxKit's ten-second complete-reply limit, 2 MiB response cap and no automatic retries. Give the new HTTP client equivalent full-read limits. |
   101	| RPC lifetime | Common Practice acquires its RPC client once. | Keep TaxKit's per-operation client scope: a receive loop left on an earlier Cloudflare request can stall the next request. Copying the once-acquired loop would undo a deliberate fix. |
   102	| Documentation | HTTP has selected content/Markdown/SEO/image operations. | TaxKit also needs discovery, navigation, page, search and Markdown. An HTTP-only Website would need equivalent checked coverage; do not add a second content renderer. |
   103	| Package consumers | Common Practice's packages are private and source-oriented. | Keep TaxKit's compiled exports, actual packed SDK entry points and clean downstream consumer checks when those contracts change. |
   104	
   105	This resolves the Website choice for the foundation change. A later HTTP switch
   106	can be assessed on its own merit; it is not required to adopt Common Practice.
   107	
   108	## Cloudflare first, with host-independent packages
   109	
   110	Use Effect services and Layers to describe shared operations and supply their
   111	implementations. Core, rule, calculator and transport packages must not import
   112	Cloudflare, Alchemy or Bun server code, interpret trusted Cloudflare headers, or
   113	run Effects themselves. The SDK's private Promise adapter is a justified public
   114	library execution boundary.
   115	
   116	The API app owns the host adapters. Cloudflare supplies native request context,
   117	private bindings, rate services and sessions. Bun supplies its HTTP server and
   118	configuration through one top-level runner. Both use the same tax operations.
   119	Do not add a managed Promise runtime to the native API Worker.
   120	
   121	Matching upstream Effect 4.0.2 supports this separation: `HttpApiBuilder` captures
   122	shared services, `HttpRouter` supplies the current request scope, and
   123	`BunHttpServer` supplies the abstract server. `HttpRouter.provideRequest` builds
   124	its supplied Layer per request; it must not own an application-wide capacity
   125	pool. Alchemy's Worker bridge builds the application once and supplies native
   126	request context. Stream cleanup belongs to the current consumer; isolate
   127	shutdown is not a guaranteed cleanup hook.
   128	
   129	Cloudflare already captures one bounded calculation service. Keep its shared
   130	eight-place pool, five-second work budget, exact Website Origin and checked
   131	private identity. A timer cannot interrupt synchronous calculation code.
   132	
   133	Bun currently builds the bounded service per request, creating a fresh pool for
   134	each one. Fix that at Bun application composition after the Cloudflare work.
   135	Keep its current HTTP coverage and explicitly owned CORS/admission differences;
   136	no Cloudflare Durable Object substitute or new Bun protocol promise is needed.
   137	
   138	## Patch-free Alchemy design
   139	
   140	TaxKit currently locks Effect 4.0.0 and patched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.80. Common
   141	Practice locks Effect 4.0.2 and unpatched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.81. The target is the
   142	compatible, published, unpatched upstream package used by Common Practice,
   143	checked against TaxKit's installed types and consumers during implementation.
   144	An upstream comparison is not an installation or a completed upgrade.
   145	
   146	Two declarations need to change before removing the current Alchemy patch:
   147	
   148	1. **Remove the two-way output dependency.** In
   149	   `packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.ts`, Website uses API output/binding
   150	   while API reads Website output. Replace API's reverse dependency with one
   151	   checked, stage-owned exact Website address. The same settings own its domain
   152	   or checked Worker name. For Preview, retain the actual existing Worker name
   153	   and use Alchemy's native checked account-subdomain setting; do not guess the
   154	   generated hostname or add Preview DNS as an incidental change. API retains
   155	   its own `Worker.URL`; Website consumes
   156	   API output and retains its own `Worker.URL`. Declare API, then Website.
   157	   Confirm native local development addresses before implementation: local ports
   158	   can be assigned at runtime. Do not widen allowed Origins to `*` or infer an
   159	   address from arbitrary request headers to solve this.
   160	2. **Avoid the shared redirect write.** Remove `domain.redirects` from the
   161	   Website declaration. Attach the native apex and `www` domain aliases to the
   162	   Website, then return the existing permanent redirect to the canonical apex
   163	   at Website ingress, before routes or calculator forms. Preserve path/query
   164	   semantics and the current redirect status. This bypasses the Worker
   165	   provider's shared-zone redirect ruleset code without a custom provider.
   166	   Common Practice itself uses `domain.redirects`; this field is a necessary
   167	   TaxKit departure. Previously saved redirect declarations can invoke the
   168	   same provider path during removal, so check the existing-state transition
   169	   before calling the migration safe. No patched replacement is permitted.
   170	
   171	Upstream beta.81 still treats every shared redirect-rules read failure as an
   172	absent ruleset. The earlier mocked forbidden-read case produced a replacement
   173	write. That shows a problem with blindly keeping this declaration while deleting
   174	the patch; it does not require retaining the patch. A separate native Ruleset
   175	resource owns an entire zone phase, so it is unsuitable unless TaxKit owns every
   176	rule in that phase. Use the Website alias/redirect approach instead.
   177	
   178	Remove the Alchemy entry from `patchedDependencies`, its patch file, and the
   179	corresponding lockfile patch references together. Search build, install and
   180	infrastructure code for every other Alchemy modification. Do not relocate a fix
   181	into a wrapper, copied source or postinstall step. Preserve logical resource IDs,
   182	stack/state identities and the existing unrelated DNS records.
   183	
   184	The Atom scheduler peer-metadata patch is unrelated to Alchemy. Common Practice
   185	also has non-Alchemy Effect/PostHog patches; those are not required by this
   186	proposal and must not be copied without a TaxKit need. Align the Effect family
   187	and explicit companion override if choosing 4.0.2. Any React/Atom compatibility
   188	change needs ordinary type/build/browser checks, not a new exception receipt.
   189	
   190	## Ordinary commits, deployments and Doppler
   191	
   192	Copy Common Practice's workflow shape:
   193	
   194	- Make normal coherent Git commits and PRs. Describe the change and meaningful
   195	  test results in the PR. Do not require an approval JSON, finding crosswalk,
   196	  source-digest receipt or separate commit acceptance ceremony.
   197	- Run one ordinary check workflow. Use the same verification command locally
   198	  and in Actions, rather than a second release-policy graph that rechecks every
   199	  earlier document and receipt.
   200	- On an internal PR, install the frozen lockfile, check the change, then run
   201	  native Alchemy dry-run and deploy for that PR's stage. Check the Website/API.
   202	  On close, use native destroy restricted to that PR stage. Keep fork secrets
   203	  excluded, same-stage deployment/cleanup serialised, and the current PR-state
   204	  check. These prevent real mistakes and are small enough to understand.
   205	- Production runs manually from `main`: ordinary verification, native dry-run,
   206	  native deploy, native drift, and a small public Website/API check. Use existing
   207	  GitHub environment settings; do not add a second TaxKit approval system.
   208	- Use native `Doppler.Secrets`, `.env` and disabled `ProcessEnv` fallback in one
   209	  owner, following Common Practice. `.env` overrides also apply in hosted runs;
   210	  Actions should write deployment metadata only. Retain TaxKit's actual Doppler
   211	  project/config mapping and environment-scoped read-only Doppler credentials.
   212	  Do not copy another project's values or duplicate Cloudflare keys in GitHub.
   213	- Roll back by redeploying the previous working Git revision through the same
   214	  native workflow. Alchemy resource retention is not a deployment snapshot.
   215	
   216	Target scripts are short native commands such as `dev`, `pr:plan`, `pr:deploy`,
   217	`pr:destroy`, `production:plan`, `production:deploy` and `production:drift`.
   218	The names can match Common Practice while selecting TaxKit's existing `prod`
   219	and `pr-N` state identities. Do not rename a live stack/stage as a side effect
   220	of making commands prettier. Native local development still needs its exact
   221	address and state behaviour checked; delete custom wrappers once their useful
   222	behaviour is covered by the native entrypoint.
   223	
   224	GitHub records the commit and run; Alchemy records state; the smoke check
   225	confirms the deployed endpoints. No separate receipt workflow, deployment
   226	manifest, hash catalogue, custody packet or per-step approval file is needed.
   227	A request to review the design does not itself deploy it, delete resources or
   228	rotate secrets, but those ordinary task boundaries do not need a bespoke record
   229	system. Current Actions credit availability has not been rechecked here.
   230	
   231	## Remove ceremony at its source
   232	
   233	The implementation must remove requirements, callers and tests together, rather
   234	than disable a failing check while leaving its policy active.
   235	
   236	| Current owner | Proposed retirement or simplification |
   237	| --- | --- |
   238	| `.github/workflows/docs-deployment-workflow-receipts.yml` | Delete the receipt reconciliation workflow entirely. |
   239	| Four retired `docs-preview`, `docs-preview-teardown`, `docs-production`, `docs-production-hosted-verify` workflow stubs | Replace obsolete app workflow routing with the current native preview/production workflows; no workflow whose only role is announcing a retirement. |
   240	| `tools/docs-deployment` and root `check:docs-deployment-*`, `check:doppler-custody`, retired docs dev commands | Remove custody, workflow-input/run/plan/teardown receipt validation, source-hash admission, custom plan projections, old-app wrappers and their tests. Do not move this machinery to a newly named folder. |
   241	| `tools/governance`, `tools/evals/hgi-206`, `tools/evals/harness-foundation` | Remove audit acceptance, skill-receipt, epoch/requalification and harness-record enforcement from normal development, including their validators and fixtures. |
   242	| `tools/quality-workflow`, Quality workflow and `turbo.json` | Remove bespoke control/automation registers, release-evidence admission and tests of that paperwork. Replace Quality with ordinary checks; delete orphan tasks and cache outputs. |
   243	| `tools/documentation/runbook-*`, `runbook-contract.json` | Remove enforced runbook counts, authority/receipt cross-reconciliation and generated validation reports. Keep a short human deployment/recovery procedure. |
   244	| `tools/documentation/owner-policy.json`, documentation policy and schemas | Keep useful links, commands, metadata/source checks. Remove mandatory acceptance receipts, source hashes and historical evidence validation; simplify public page status to its actual content/navigation owner. |
   245	| `tools/documentation/catalogue.*`, `packages/docs-content`, `packages/docs-fumadocs` | Preserve actual content compilation, generated source and Website catalogue loading. Replace acceptance-record plumbing without deleting the working public documentation product. |
   246	| `packages/scripts/src/release-readiness`, `release:present` and custom `release:check` | Remove per-run authority envelopes, proof graphs, digest-ledger outputs and deploy/receipt prerequisites. Preserve real build, package packing and downstream checks as direct commands when releasing or changing package contracts. `@taxkit/scripts` exports this runner: check its consumers before retiring those exports deliberately. |
   247	| `AGENTS.md`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/operations/authority-model.md`, standards, skill profiles and active plans | Replace mandatory receipt/approval/epoch language and accumulated historical task routing with short current instructions. Keep tax/package boundaries, ordinary operation scope and a practical rollback command. |
   248	| New audit packet from this review | Remove inventories, scope/findings JSON, acceptance/impact crosswalks, registry/provider result packets and validation hashes. Retain the useful findings and source comparison in this proposal. |
   249	
   250	Two build/test dependencies need replacement before deleting their old owners:
   251	`packages/docs-content` currently builds its catalogue from acceptance records
   252	and hashes; switch to the reviewed MDX/frontmatter/navigation sources while
   253	keeping generated catalogue consumers working. Native app-stack tests read two
   254	plan fixtures under `tools/docs-deployment`; retain useful resource cases under
   255	their actual test owner.
   256	
   257	Older history is already recorded in Git. It must stop being an input to current
   258	checks, a prerequisite for new work or a reason to add another retention
   259	manifest. This design edit removes only its own new uncommitted packet; removal
   260	of existing tools and old files belongs to the implementation. Do not delete
   261	unrelated source, secrets or active runtime assets under a broad folder name.
   262	
   263	## Checks that still earn their place
   264	
   265	The target verification command follows Common Practice: build, format, lint,
   266	types, Effect diagnostics, tests, unused-code and a small docs check. Retain
   267	nested-workspace import/export enforcement and actual tax/schema/API tests.
   268	Keep resource-stage validation and fork-secret exclusion in their ordinary
   269	owners. Remove duplicated checks and every test whose only purpose is enforcing
   270	the retired paperwork.
   271	
   272	Run focused native Website/API tests when changing those apps, bindings or
   273	client lifetime. Run SDK packing and clean downstream checks when changing its
   274	exports or supported dependencies. Keep local emulator tests separate from
   275	provider-mutating integration tests; Common Practice's live integration tests
   276	are opt-in. Do not run the whole native suite after every wording change, nor
   277	turn a failed meaningful runtime check into a passing result by dropping its
   278	assertion or increasing its timeout without understanding the failure.
   279	
   280	Normal Changesets still describe public package contract changes. The existing
   281	fixed version group is a packaging choice, not a deployment approval system;
   282	this change does not need to redesign it. Drop per-run versioning authority
   283	receipts and requirements to version private infrastructure for ordinary app
   284	work. No package contract changes in this document-only edit need a Changeset.
   285	
"}

     1	# Strict Effect and lint policy
     2	
     3	All owned TypeScript, JSX, configuration, command programs and tests pass through
     4	Oxlint. The starting presets are current Ultracite core, React and Vitest. Effect
     5	language-service diagnostics run separately because its current Oxlint patch
     6	does not support Oxlint 1.85. TypeScript checks owned code in strict mode.
     7	
     8	The entire Site `tools/oxlint` directory is retained under
     9	`tools/oxlint/vendor/site`, including all Effect, Bun, MDX, Site and anti-slop
    10	extensions and their upstream test sources. The active config enables every
    11	Site rule, with narrowly recorded boundary exceptions below. MDX and other
    12	future-facing rules are active even when there are no matching features yet.
    13	
    14	Other retained sources are Commonplace, Bundjil, Adad, Learned, TaxKit and
    15	Pollsor, plus the strict-effect-ts portable policy from Commonplace PR 27. Their generic Effect and
    16	ownership plugins extend the active rule set.
    17	The native Alchemy secrets policy is a separate unchanged asset from Commonplace.
    18	Its source revision and hash are recorded with the other retained files.
    19	Common Practice additionally forbids computed bracket access and native `.at()` so lookups cannot sneak
    20	through a successful typecheck. Use Effect Array/Record and handle absence.
    21	Oxlint's built-in `no-ternary` rule rejects every ternary. Use `Option.match` when a value may be absent,
    22	`Boolean.match` for yes/no decisions, and `Match` for richer choices. Branch on
    23	a closed literal union with `Match.value` and `Match.exhaustive`, not a
    24	`Boolean.match` over one member, so a new member fails to compile. `Option`
    25	must not be introduced merely to represent a boolean decision.
    26	
    27	## Reference preservation
    28	
    29	Vendor files are unchanged snapshots, not Common Practice-owned implementation. Their
    30	native JS/TS techniques are an explicit import exception, not permission to
    31	write Common Practice that way. Vendor sources and deliberately forbidden fixture inputs
    32	are excluded from normal lint/type checks. The positive/negative fixtures run
    33	through the actual config at temporary paths; tests require one file examined,
    34	a failing exit for prohibited code, and a clean exit for valid Effect code.
    35	
    36	[Source revisions](../sources/lint-provenance.txt) and
    37	[file hashes](../sources/lint-vendor.sha256) identify the imported content.
    38	Old source tests are retained for reference, not counted as passing Common Practice tests.
    39	Some expect the original repo's files and cannot run unchanged here.
    40	
    41	Tests that start several real lint commands in sequence have a 30-second
    42	limit; the 24-command Promise-boundary test has 60 seconds. These limits allow
    43	the command batches to finish on a busy machine. Ordinary tests keep their
    44	default limit. Required diagnostics, rejection counts and clean exits are
    45	unchanged.
    46	
    47	## Deliberate rule decisions
    48	
    49	- Commonplace `no-runtime-execution-outside-main` hard-codes its CLI path.
    50	  It is off; Site, Bundjil, Learned and TaxKit check Common Practice runtime ownership.
    51	- Learned `no-native-array-methods` reports `Effect.flatMap` as a native array
    52	  method. It is off; Site's native-array rule and all data-first collection
    53	  prohibitions remain active.
    54	- Strict Effect's `no-imperative-collections` rejects loops, reassignment,
    55	  native collection methods, transient mutation and manual closed-union matching.
    56	  Sequential work uses `Effect.forEach` with concurrency 1; synchronous
    57	  traversal uses Effect Array functions. The other ten portable rules remain
    58	  off because the existing rules already cover their prohibitions.
    59	  `unicorn/no-array-for-each` and `unicorn/no-array-sort` are replaced by this
    60	  check: those name-only checks reject Effect functions as though they were
    61	  native array methods. The replacement still rejects native `forEach`, `sort`
    62	  and `toSorted`; the real-command fixtures prove rejection and acceptance.
    63	  Imported `alchemy/Namespace.push` is also accepted: upstream implements it
    64	  by providing an Effect service, without changing a collection. Commonplace's
    65	  command fixtures reject the same method from another library or a shadowed
    66	  import. No method allowance or disabled rule is needed.
    67	  Its only assignment allowance is the exact
    68	  `globalThis.__ALCHEMY_RUNTIME__` target in
    69	  `apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/entry.test.ts`. Alchemy replaces this flag
    70	  when bundling. The unbundled startup test sets it within
    71	  `Effect.acquireUseRelease` and restores it on failure or success. The fixture
    72	  proves that the same assignment at a nearby path is still rejected.
    73	- TaxKit `no-host-imports-in-contracts` is on except runtime entry files and
    74	  Effect tests, which provide the platform services. Its runtime-name rule is
    75	  similarly scoped because it only recognises TaxKit's original paths. The
    76	  three other runtime rules remain active on these files.
    77	- Schema decoding is permitted only in the Alchemy entry, website resource
    78	  declaration, reference/file input adapters, the exact publishing ingress/egress
    79	  adapters listed below, and tests. Code outside those
    80	  paths cannot execute Schema decoders. Expected failures stay typed; no
    81	  blanket `orDie` conversion is used.
    82	  `packages/content/src/body.ingress.ts` is the exact authored Markdown body
    83	  parser: it checks captured headings, paragraphs and sections before they
    84	  become Page data. Its malformed-block and duplicate-section cases are tested.
    85	- Commonplace's package-boundary implementation is active. The equivalent
    86	  retained Bundjil/Learned/Pollsor/TaxKit package plugins are duplicate source
    87	  references rather than additional checks.
    88	- TaxKit's `taxkit-rules.js` is retained only. Its application-specific adapters,
    89	  imports and domain rules do not describe Common Practice. Commonplace's Bun rules are
    90	  retained as overlapping reference; all Site Bun rules are active.
    91	- Site's presentational preferences for function declarations, key ordering,
    92	  named generator functions, inline comments and declaration order are retained:
    93	  these are off. TypeScript's generic `consistent-return` is off because it
    94	  misreads `yield*` of typed failures. This does not disable checked Effect
    95	  error handling or unsafe type/Promise rules.
    96	- The formatter skips unchanged vendor files, vendored skills, generated routes,
    97	  build output and lockfiles. Knip's font exceptions cover CSS `@import` assets;
    98	  `@effect/language-service` is provided by @effect/tsgo, not a missing package.
    99	  These are explicit dependency-analysis
   100	  exceptions, not ignored app modules.
   101	
   102	- Agent worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` are Git-ignored. Each is a full
   103	  checkout with its own `oxlint.config.ts` and `.oxfmtrc.json`. The
   104	  `.claude/**` ignore patterns skip their files, but Oxlint still loaded a
   105	  nested config (failing on a duplicate `common-practice` plugin) and Oxfmt still checked
   106	  their files. Both tools walk the tree through `.gitignore`, so the ignore
   107	  entry stops both. Root checks therefore cover only this checkout.
   108	
   109	No rule can replace review of a boundary's meaning. Treat a passing check as
   110	proof of that check, not proof that every future architecture choice is sound.
   111	
   112	## Static Layers
   113	
   114	Owned Effect Layers are static values. Supply their dependencies through the
   115	Requirements type channel: this tells Effect which services a Layer needs.
   116	Callers provide those services with native `Layer.succeed`; tests can replace
   117	implementations with `Layer.mock` or another static Layer. There are no
   118	grandfathered factory exceptions.
   119	
   120	`common-practice/static-layers` rejects functions returning known Layers,
   121	including constructor aliases, curried constructors, Layer-preserving pipes,
   122	native HTTP router builders and Layer return types. It follows local constants,
   123	type aliases and scoped imports so a shadowed name cannot borrow an import's
   124	identity. Inline callbacks used by native composition remain valid, as do
   125	functions returning Effects or scoped test fixture bundles.
   126	
   127	The rule checks syntax; it cannot infer the result of every imported helper.
   128	Opaque results still need clear owning types and review. Real Oxlint command
   129	fixtures prove factory rejection, static composition, test replacement and
   130	shadowed-import handling. No automatic fix moves dependencies for the author.
   131	
   132	## Native Alchemy secret sources
   133	
   134	The three `alchemy-secrets` rules apply to owned code:
   135	
   136	- `native-sources` requires recognised local Doppler lists to contain Doppler,
   137	  then dotenv, then an explicitly disabled shell provider. It also rejects
   138	  recognised enabled or implicit shell providers.
   139	- `explicit-stack-sources` rejects configured native Stack calls without a
   140	  locally inspectable `secrets` field, including empty lists and missing values.
   141	- `no-doppler-wrapper` rejects recognised Effect child-process calls that run
   142	  `doppler run` directly or through a literal shell command.
   143	
   144	Actual Oxlint fixtures prove wrong-order, missing-shell, enabled-shell,
   145	missing-stack and command-wrapper rejection, plus acceptance of the declared
   146	native list. Shared tests additionally cover aliases and shadowed imports.
   147	These syntax checks do not follow imported lists, class-stack `.make`, arbitrary
   148	callbacks or shell/YAML/JSON workflows. They cannot prove token scope or actual
   149	source precedence. The infrastructure tests compose native stacks across all
   150	supported stages to prove fallback, missing `.env`, empty overrides and excluded
   151	shell values. The deployment runbook owns sign-in, stage mappings and hosted checks.

     1	# Strict Effect and lint policy
     2	
     3	All owned TypeScript, JSX, configuration, command programs and tests pass through
     4	Oxlint. The starting presets are current Ultracite core, React and Vitest. Effect
     5	language-service diagnostics run separately because its current Oxlint patch
     6	does not support Oxlint 1.85. TypeScript checks owned code in strict mode.
     7	
     8	The entire Site `tools/oxlint` directory is retained under
     9	`tools/oxlint/vendor/site`, including all Effect, Bun, MDX, Site and anti-slop
    10	extensions and their upstream test sources. The active config enables every
    11	Site rule, with narrowly recorded boundary exceptions below. MDX and other
    12	future-facing rules are active even when there are no matching features yet.
    13	
    14	Other retained sources are Commonplace, Bundjil, Adad, Learned, TaxKit and
    15	Pollsor, plus the strict-effect-ts portable policy from Commonplace PR 27. Their generic Effect and
    16	ownership plugins extend the active rule set.
    17	The native Alchemy secrets policy is a separate unchanged asset from Commonplace.
    18	Its source revision and hash are recorded with the other retained files.
    19	Common Practice additionally forbids computed bracket access and native `.at()` so lookups cannot sneak
    20	through a successful typecheck. Use Effect Array/Record and handle absence.
    21	Oxlint's built-in `no-ternary` rule rejects every ternary. Use `Option.match` when a value may be absent,
    22	`Boolean.match` for yes/no decisions, and `Match` for richer choices. Branch on
    23	a closed literal union with `Match.value` and `Match.exhaustive`, not a
    24	`Boolean.match` over one member, so a new member fails to compile. `Option`
    25	must not be introduced merely to represent a boolean decision.
    26	
    27	## Reference preservation
    28	
    29	Vendor files are unchanged snapshots, not Common Practice-owned implementation. Their
    30	native JS/TS techniques are an explicit import exception, not permission to
    31	write Common Practice that way. Vendor sources and deliberately forbidden fixture inputs
    32	are excluded from normal lint/type checks. The positive/negative fixtures run
    33	through the actual config at temporary paths; tests require one file examined,
    34	a failing exit for prohibited code, and a clean exit for valid Effect code.
    35	
    36	[Source revisions](../sources/lint-provenance.txt) and
    37	[file hashes](../sources/lint-vendor.sha256) identify the imported content.
    38	Old source tests are retained for reference, not counted as passing Common Practice tests.
    39	Some expect the original repo's files and cannot run unchanged here.
    40	
    41	Tests that start several real lint commands in sequence have a 30-second
    42	limit; the 24-command Promise-boundary test has 60 seconds. These limits allow
    43	the command batches to finish on a busy machine. Ordinary tests keep their
    44	default limit. Required diagnostics, rejection counts and clean exits are
    45	unchanged.
    46	
    47	## Deliberate rule decisions
    48	
    49	- Commonplace `no-runtime-execution-outside-main` hard-codes its CLI path.
    50	  It is off; Site, Bundjil, Learned and TaxKit check Common Practice runtime ownership.
    51	- Learned `no-native-array-methods` reports `Effect.flatMap` as a native array
    52	  method. It is off; Site's native-array rule and all data-first collection
    53	  prohibitions remain active.
    54	- Strict Effect's `no-imperative-collections` rejects loops, reassignment,
    55	  native collection methods, transient mutation and manual closed-union matching.
    56	  Sequential work uses `Effect.forEach` with concurrency 1; synchronous
    57	  traversal uses Effect Array functions. The other ten portable rules remain
    58	  off because the existing rules already cover their prohibitions.
    59	  `unicorn/no-array-for-each` and `unicorn/no-array-sort` are replaced by this
    60	  check: those name-only checks reject Effect functions as though they were
    61	  native array methods. The replacement still rejects native `forEach`, `sort`
    62	  and `toSorted`; the real-command fixtures prove rejection and acceptance.
    63	  Imported `alchemy/Namespace.push` is also accepted: upstream implements it
    64	  by providing an Effect service, without changing a collection. Commonplace's
    65	  command fixtures reject the same method from another library or a shadowed
    66	  import. No method allowance or disabled rule is needed.
    67	  Its only assignment allowance is the exact
    68	  `globalThis.__ALCHEMY_RUNTIME__` target in
    69	  `apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/entry.test.ts`. Alchemy replaces this flag
    70	  when bundling. The unbundled startup test sets it within
    71	  `Effect.acquireUseRelease` and restores it on failure or success. The fixture
    72	  proves that the same assignment at a nearby path is still rejected.
    73	- TaxKit `no-host-imports-in-contracts` is on except runtime entry files and
    74	  Effect tests, which provide the platform services. Its runtime-name rule is
    75	  similarly scoped because it only recognises TaxKit's original paths. The
    76	  three other runtime rules remain active on these files.
    77	- Schema decoding is permitted only in the Alchemy entry, website resource
    78	  declaration, reference/file input adapters, the exact publishing ingress/egress
    79	  adapters listed below, and tests. Code outside those
    80	  paths cannot execute Schema decoders. Expected failures stay typed; no
    81	  blanket `orDie` conversion is used.
    82	  `packages/content/src/body.ingress.ts` is the exact authored Markdown body
    83	  parser: it checks captured headings, paragraphs and sections before they
    84	  become Page data. Its malformed-block and duplicate-section cases are tested.
    85	- Commonplace's package-boundary implementation is active. The equivalent
    86	  retained Bundjil/Learned/Pollsor/TaxKit package plugins are duplicate source
    87	  references rather than additional checks.
    88	- TaxKit's `taxkit-rules.js` is retained only. Its application-specific adapters,
    89	  imports and domain rules do not describe Common Practice. Commonplace's Bun rules are
    90	  retained as overlapping reference; all Site Bun rules are active.
    91	- Site's presentational preferences for function declarations, key ordering,
    92	  named generator functions, inline comments and declaration order are retained:
    93	  these are off. TypeScript's generic `consistent-return` is off because it
    94	  misreads `yield*` of typed failures. This does not disable checked Effect
    95	  error handling or unsafe type/Promise rules.
    96	- The formatter skips unchanged vendor files, vendored skills, generated routes,
    97	  build output and lockfiles. Knip's font exceptions cover CSS `@import` assets;
    98	  `@effect/language-service` is provided by @effect/tsgo, not a missing package.
    99	  These are explicit dependency-analysis
   100	  exceptions, not ignored app modules.
   101	
   102	- Agent worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` are Git-ignored. Each is a full
   103	  checkout with its own `oxlint.config.ts` and `.oxfmtrc.json`. The
   104	  `.claude/**` ignore patterns skip their files, but Oxlint still loaded a
   105	  nested config (failing on a duplicate `common-practice` plugin) and Oxfmt still checked
   106	  their files. Both tools walk the tree through `.gitignore`, so the ignore
   107	  entry stops both. Root checks therefore cover only this checkout.
   108	
   109	No rule can replace review of a boundary's meaning. Treat a passing check as
   110	proof of that check, not proof that every future architecture choice is sound.
   111	
   112	## Static Layers
   113	
   114	Owned Effect Layers are static values. Supply their dependencies through the
   115	Requirements type channel: this tells Effect which services a Layer needs.
   116	Callers provide those services with native `Layer.succeed`; tests can replace
   117	implementations with `Layer.mock` or another static Layer. There are no
   118	grandfathered factory exceptions.
   119	
   120	`common-practice/static-layers` rejects functions returning known Layers,
   121	including constructor aliases, curried constructors, Layer-preserving pipes,
   122	native HTTP router builders and Layer return types. It follows local constants,
   123	type aliases and scoped imports so a shadowed name cannot borrow an import's
   124	identity. Inline callbacks used by native composition remain valid, as do
   125	functions returning Effects or scoped test fixture bundles.
   126	
   127	The rule checks syntax; it cannot infer the result of every imported helper.
   128	Opaque results still need clear owning types and review. Real Oxlint command
   129	fixtures prove factory rejection, static composition, test replacement and
   130	shadowed-import handling. No automatic fix moves dependencies for the author.
   131	
   132	## Native Alchemy secret sources
   133	
   134	The three `alchemy-secrets` rules apply to owned code:
   135	
   136	- `native-sources` requires recognised local Doppler lists to contain Doppler,
   137	  then dotenv, then an explicitly disabled shell provider. It also rejects
   138	  recognised enabled or implicit shell providers.
   139	- `explicit-stack-sources` rejects configured native Stack calls without a
   140	  locally inspectable `secrets` field, including empty lists and missing values.
   141	- `no-doppler-wrapper` rejects recognised Effect child-process calls that run
   142	  `doppler run` directly or through a literal shell command.
   143	
   144	Actual Oxlint fixtures prove wrong-order, missing-shell, enabled-shell,
   145	missing-stack and command-wrapper rejection, plus acceptance of the declared
   146	native list. Shared tests additionally cover aliases and shadowed imports.
   147	These syntax checks do not follow imported lists, class-stack `.make`, arbitrary
   148	callbacks or shell/YAML/JSON workflows. They cannot prove token scope or actual
   149	source precedence. The infrastructure tests compose native stacks across all
   150	supported stages to prove fallback, missing `.env`, empty overrides and excluded
   151	shell values. The deployment runbook owns sign-in, stage mappings and hosted checks.

     3	All owned TypeScript, JSX, configuration, command programs and tests pass through
     4	Oxlint. The starting presets are current Ultracite core, React and Vitest. Effect
     5	language-service diagnostics run separately because its current Oxlint patch
     6	does not support Oxlint 1.85. TypeScript checks owned code in strict mode.
     7	
     8	The entire Site `tools/oxlint` directory is retained under
     9	`tools/oxlint/vendor/site`, including all Effect, Bun, MDX, Site and anti-slop
    10	extensions and their upstream test sources. The active config enables every
    11	Site rule, with narrowly recorded boundary exceptions below. MDX and other
    12	future-facing rules are active even when there are no matching features yet.
    13	
    14	Other retained sources are Commonplace, Bundjil, Adad, Learned, TaxKit and
    15	Pollsor, plus the strict-effect-ts portable policy from Commonplace PR 27. Their generic Effect and
    16	ownership plugins extend the active rule set.
    17	The native Alchemy secrets policy is a separate unchanged asset from Commonplace.
    18	Its source revision and hash are recorded with the other retained files.
    19	Common Practice additionally forbids computed bracket access and native `.at()` so lookups cannot sneak
    20	through a successful typecheck. Use Effect Array/Record and handle absence.
    21	Oxlint's built-in `no-ternary` rule rejects every ternary. Use `Option.match` when a value may be absent,
    22	`Boolean.match` for yes/no decisions, and `Match` for richer choices. Branch on
    23	a closed literal union with `Match.value` and `Match.exhaustive`, not a
    24	`Boolean.match` over one member, so a new member fails to compile. `Option`
    25	must not be introduced merely to represent a boolean decision.
    26	
    27	## Reference preservation
    28	
    29	Vendor files are unchanged snapshots, not Common Practice-owned implementation. Their
    30	native JS/TS techniques are an explicit import exception, not permission to
    31	write Common Practice that way. Vendor sources and deliberately forbidden fixture inputs
    32	are excluded from normal lint/type checks. The positive/negative fixtures run
    33	through the actual config at temporary paths; tests require one file examined,
    34	a failing exit for prohibited code, and a clean exit for valid Effect code.
    35	
    36	[Source revisions](../sources/lint-provenance.txt) and
    37	[file hashes](../sources/lint-vendor.sha256) identify the imported content.
    38	Old source tests are retained for reference, not counted as passing Common Practice tests.
    39	Some expect the original repo's files and cannot run unchanged here.
    40	
    41	Tests that start several real lint commands in sequence have a 30-second
    42	limit; the 24-command Promise-boundary test has 60 seconds. These limits allow
    43	the command batches to finish on a busy machine. Ordinary tests keep their
    44	default limit. Required diagnostics, rejection counts and clean exits are
    45	unchanged.
    46	
    47	## Deliberate rule decisions
    48	
    49	- Commonplace `no-runtime-execution-outside-main` hard-codes its CLI path.
    50	  It is off; Site, Bundjil, Learned and TaxKit check Common Practice runtime ownership.
    51	- Learned `no-native-array-methods` reports `Effect.flatMap` as a native array
    52	  method. It is off; Site's native-array rule and all data-first collection
    53	  prohibitions remain active.
    54	- Strict Effect's `no-imperative-collections` rejects loops, reassignment,
    55	  native collection methods, transient mutation and manual closed-union matching.
    56	  Sequential work uses `Effect.forEach` with concurrency 1; synchronous
    57	  traversal uses Effect Array functions. The other ten portable rules remain
    58	  off because the existing rules already cover their prohibitions.
    59	  `unicorn/no-array-for-each` and `unicorn/no-array-sort` are replaced by this
    60	  check: those name-only checks reject Effect functions as though they were
    61	  native array methods. The replacement still rejects native `forEach`, `sort`
    62	  and `toSorted`; the real-command fixtures prove rejection and acceptance.
    63	  Imported `alchemy/Namespace.push` is also accepted: upstream implements it
    64	  by providing an Effect service, without changing a collection. Commonplace's
    65	  command fixtures reject the same method from another library or a shadowed
    66	  import. No method allowance or disabled rule is needed.
    67	  Its only assignment allowance is the exact
    68	  `globalThis.__ALCHEMY_RUNTIME__` target in
    69	  `apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/entry.test.ts`. Alchemy replaces this flag
    70	  when bundling. The unbundled startup test sets it within
    71	  `Effect.acquireUseRelease` and restores it on failure or success. The fixture
    72	  proves that the same assignment at a nearby path is still rejected.
    73	- TaxKit `no-host-imports-in-contracts` is on except runtime entry files and
    74	  Effect tests, which provide the platform services. Its runtime-name rule is
    75	  similarly scoped because it only recognises TaxKit's original paths. The
    76	  three other runtime rules remain active on these files.
    77	- Schema decoding is permitted only in the Alchemy entry, website resource
    78	  declaration, reference/file input adapters, the exact publishing ingress/egress
    79	  adapters listed below, and tests. Code outside those
    80	  paths cannot execute Schema decoders. Expected failures stay typed; no
    81	  blanket `orDie` conversion is used.
    82	  `packages/content/src/body.ingress.ts` is the exact authored Markdown body
    83	  parser: it checks captured headings, paragraphs and sections before they
    84	  become Page data. Its malformed-block and duplicate-section cases are tested.
    85	- Commonplace's package-boundary implementation is active. The equivalent
    86	  retained Bundjil/Learned/Pollsor/TaxKit package plugins are duplicate source
    87	  references rather than additional checks.
    88	- TaxKit's `taxkit-rules.js` is retained only. Its application-specific adapters,
    89	  imports and domain rules do not describe Common Practice. Commonplace's Bun rules are
    90	  retained as overlapping reference; all Site Bun rules are active.
    91	- Site's presentational preferences for function declarations, key ordering,
    92	  named generator functions, inline comments and declaration order are retained:
    93	  these are off. TypeScript's generic `consistent-return` is off because it
    94	  misreads `yield*` of typed failures. This does not disable checked Effect
    95	  error handling or unsafe type/Promise rules.
    96	- The formatter skips unchanged vendor files, vendored skills, generated routes,
    97	  build output and lockfiles. Knip's font exceptions cover CSS `@import` assets;
    98	  `@effect/language-service` is provided by @effect/tsgo, not a missing package.
    99	  These are explicit dependency-analysis
   100	  exceptions, not ignored app modules.
   101	
   102	- Agent worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` are Git-ignored. Each is a full
   103	  checkout with its own `oxlint.config.ts` and `.oxfmtrc.json`. The
   104	  `.claude/**` ignore patterns skip their files, but Oxlint still loaded a
   105	  nested config (failing on a duplicate `common-practice` plugin) and Oxfmt still checked
   106	  their files. Both tools walk the tree through `.gitignore`, so the ignore
   107	  entry stops both. Root checks therefore cover only this checkout.
   108	
   109	No rule can replace review of a boundary's meaning. Treat a passing check as
   110	proof of that check, not proof that every future architecture choice is sound.
   111	
   112	## Static Layers
   113	
   114	Owned Effect Layers are static values. Supply their dependencies through the
   115	Requirements type channel: this tells Effect which services a Layer needs.
   116	Callers provide those services with native `Layer.succeed`; tests can replace
   117	implementations with `Layer.mock` or another static Layer. There are no
   118	grandfathered factory exceptions.
   119	
   120	`common-practice/static-layers` rejects functions returning known Layers,
   121	including constructor aliases, curried constructors, Layer-preserving pipes,
   122	native HTTP router builders and Layer return types. It follows local constants,
   123	type aliases and scoped imports so a shadowed name cannot borrow an import's
   124	identity. Inline callbacks used by native composition remain valid, as do
   125	functions returning Effects or scoped test fixture bundles.
   126	
   127	The rule checks syntax; it cannot infer the result of every imported helper.
   128	Opaque results still need clear owning types and review. Real Oxlint command
   129	fixtures prove factory rejection, static composition, test replacement and
   130	shadowed-import handling. No automatic fix moves dependencies for the author.
   131	
   132	## Native Alchemy secret sources
   133	
   134	The three `alchemy-secrets` rules apply to owned code:
   135	
   136	- `native-sources` requires recognised local Doppler lists to contain Doppler,
   137	  then dotenv, then an explicitly disabled shell provider. It also rejects
   138	  recognised enabled or implicit shell providers.
   139	- `explicit-stack-sources` rejects configured native Stack calls without a
   140	  locally inspectable `secrets` field, including empty lists and missing values.
   141	- `no-doppler-wrapper` rejects recognised Effect child-process calls that run
   142	  `doppler run` directly or through a literal shell command.
   143	
   144	Actual Oxlint fixtures prove wrong-order, missing-shell, enabled-shell,
   145	missing-stack and command-wrapper rejection, plus acceptance of the declared
   146	native list. Shared tests additionally cover aliases and shadowed imports.
   147	These syntax checks do not follow imported lists, class-stack `.make`, arbitrary
   148	callbacks or shell/YAML/JSON workflows. They cannot prove token scope or actual
   149	source precedence. The infrastructure tests compose native stacks across all
   150	supported stages to prove fallback, missing `.env`, empty overrides and excluded
   151	shell values. The deployment runbook owns sign-in, stage mappings and hosted checks.
   152
