    20	   [repository audit router](references/repository-audit.md), then load its
    21	   [workflow](references/audit/workflow.md),
    22	   [corpus and journeys](references/audit/corpus-and-journeys.md),
    23	   [lenses](references/audit/lenses.md),
    24	   [findings and acceptance](references/audit/findings-and-acceptance.md), and
    25	   [variation and stopping](references/audit/variation-and-stopping.md).
    26	   Then read the
    27	   [repository contract](references/repository-contract.md),
    28	   [TanStack and Effect architecture](references/tanstack-effect.md), and
    29	   [tooling and docs](references/tooling-and-docs.md).
    30	4. Load the canonical sibling
    31	   [`package-structure`](../package-structure/SKILL.md) and
    32	   [`docs-maintainer`](../docs-maintainer/SKILL.md) skills. Resolve them
    33	   relative to this installed skill collection, or pass the skill collection
    34	   explicitly to the renderer. Stop before rendering if either is unavailable;
    35	   do not invent package/document contracts or assume a user's home directory.
    36	
    37	## Audit an existing repository
    38	
    39	Default to report-first. Define the target revision, claimed jobs, accepted
    40	outcomes, proof boundaries, authority, exclusions, and stop conditions. Account
    41	for the repository corpus, then follow a small set of representative jobs from
    42	request through ownership, implementation, proof, delivery, and acceptance.
    43	Use prior collaboration evidence when available and authorized; treat it as
    44	trajectory evidence rather than repository policy.
    45	
    46	For a whole-repository audit, create the structured scope and finding artifacts
    47	from `assets/audit/`; do not use free-form prose as the sole audit record.
    48	Validate them with `scripts/validate_audit_artifacts.py`. Return a
    49	consequence-ordered Markdown view with stable IDs, separate important
    50	corrections from optional improvements, identify the earliest owning
    51	correction, and name duplicated machinery to retire. Stop for acceptance before
    52	implementation unless the original request authorizes both. Record accepted
    53	finding IDs in the crosswalk, hand them to `prd-writer`, then use `prd-review`
    54	and `prd-implementer`.
    55	
    56	For most repositories, stop after the structural and trajectory audit,
    57	accepted important corrections, normal repository checks, and one fresh
    58	independent review. Do not create a comparative harness evaluation unless the
    59	claim is that a particular intervention changes future worker behavior.
    60	
    61	## Resolve or select versions
    62	
    63	Rendering is offline and deterministic. The checked-in snapshot is a known-good
    64	fallback, not permission to call it current. To research a refresh, use primary
    65	registries/official sources and DeepWiki only for upstream packages—not the
    66	local codebase:
    67	
    68	```bash
    69	python3 scripts/resolve_versions.py --output /tmp/provisional-versions.json
    70	```
    71	
    72	Effect ecosystem packages share the qualified exact stable v4 version, currently
    73	`4.0.2`. Resolve that exact version; registry `latest`/`beta` tags do not
    74	select the qualified native Alchemy combination. TanStack Start and Router
    75	resolve independently. Never emit `latest`.
    76	Alchemy beta and the preview-only Cloudflare scaffold require an explicit
    77	qualified/rejected decision; never infer compatibility from a registry tag.
    78	Read [version policy](references/version-policy.md); a snapshot is adopted only
    79	after full compatibility rendering and verification.
    80	
    81	## Render safely
    82	
    83	The target must be an absolute, new path. There is no overwrite mode:
    84	
    85	```bash
    86	python3 scripts/render_repository.py \
    87	  --target /absolute/new/repository \
    88	  --name example \
    89	  --scope @example \
    90	  --source-condition @example/source \
    91	  --versions assets/version-snapshot.json
    92	```
    93	
    94	The renderer stages root/app/docs/tooling assets, invokes the canonical package
    95	renderer for domain, RPC, and HTTP API packages, copies every complete current
    96	repository-skill folder, adds only the declared repository-local profiles,
    97	creates `.claude/skills/**` links to `.agents/skills/**`, validates the copied
    98	trees against their canonical sources, then atomically renames. It never
    99	templates lockfiles, generated route trees, output, caches, or dependency trees.
   100	
   101	Every scaffold includes the minimum repository-owned harness:
   102	
   103	- fixed invariant and audit guidance inside the copied local skills;
   104	- a repository harness profile as the sole local variation surface;
   105	- one docs router and documentation owner map;
   106	- structured audit scope, finding, and accepted-finding templates plus schemas;
   107	- critical journeys, proof and bounded-receipt contracts;
   108	- authority, feedback/control, automation, epoch, effectiveness, evidence, and
   109	  runbook owners;
   110	- deterministic governance and audit validation; and
   111	- an active bootstrap-harness task that qualifies the rendered defaults before
   112	  they become current repository truth.
   113	
   114	The render receipt records official sources, selected versions, compatibility
   115	decisions, config digests, limitations, and an explicitly absent lockfile. After
   116	the first `bun install`, run `scripts/finalize_repository_receipt.py` to bind the
   117	receipt to `bun.lock`; do not claim a bootstrapped fixture before that phase.
   118	
   119	Use `--skills-root /absolute/skill-collection` only when the sibling skills are
   120	installed outside the default collection. Generated repository-local skills
   121	must remain useful without that global collection after rendering. Each copied
   122	skill is the complete canonical folder. The docs-maintainer and
   123	package-structure skills receive explicit generated repository profiles; those
   124	profiles are the only permitted tree differences. Claude compatibility
   125	surfaces are links, never independently maintained copies.
   126	
   127	Include the complete `linear` skill because PRD Implementer loads it for
   128	projects with Linear tracking. The generated receipt and local validator must
   129	cover that folder and its Claude link too; a global installed copy does not
   130	satisfy the generated repository's local references.
   131	
   132	## Split folders and files by durable ownership
   133	
   134	Choose paths from the call graph and semantic owner. A repository/package
   135	boundary is justified by an independent contract; an app-internal subfolder is
   136	justified by a durable capability, domain, adapter, authority, runtime, or
   137	independently tested policy. File count alone is not a boundary, and a one-file
   138	capability should stay a file when a folder would add no meaning.
   139	
   140	- Start with actual callers, exports, tests, untrusted ingress, runtime
   141	  composition, and provider/authority edges before moving a file.
   142	- Name folders after capabilities/domains (`observability`, `cloudflare`, or
   143	  `metrics-token-qualification`) and files after owned roles (`schemas.ts`,
   144	  `errors.ts`, `service.ts`, `plan.ts`, `authority.ts`, `website.ts`, or
   145	  `manifest.main.ts`).
   163	The receiving repository owns its workspace import rule and generated export
   164	inventory. Enforce imports, re-exports and literal dynamic imports: packages
   165	cannot depend on apps, and frontend code may import domain contracts and
   166	transport clients rather than backend handlers, source loaders or live domain
   167	implementations. Derive public export facts from manifests and keep a separate
   168	explicit frontend policy. A successful typecheck alone cannot prove this
   169	direction: a forbidden app export can still be valid TypeScript.
   170	
   171	Merge these entries into the existing config; do not replace its other checks.
   172	When replacing `unicorn/throw-new-error`, turn off only that overlapping rule
   173	and record why. Keep prohibitions on throwing enabled.
   174	
   175	| Check                     | Policy and limits                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
   176	| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   177	| `no-unchecked-index`      | Rejects all computed member reads, including literal keys. Use Effect Array/Record lookup and handle absence. Adopt this stricter policy deliberately; an unavoidable host access needs an exact exception.                                                                                                                                     |
   178	| `no-native-at`            | Rejects reads/calls/aliases of `.at`; computed spellings are caught by the lookup rule. It matches the property name, not the receiver's inferred type.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
   179	| `runtime-file-convention` | Rejects unqualified/reversed runtime filenames under configured source roots. Use `runtime.server.ts` and `runtime.client.ts`. A production browser build separately checks imports.                                                                                                                                                            |
   180	| `tagged-error-name`       | Requires the class, self type and literal tag to agree. Recognises the current Schema.TaggedError factory through named/aliased/namespace/root imports.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
   181	| `error-constructor-new`   | Requires `new` for `*Error` constructors, while allowing imported `Schema.TaggedError`, `Schema.Error` and `Data.TaggedError` class factories. Type-only imports and local functions do not grant the factory exception.                                                                                                                        |
   182	| `no-promise-workflow`     | Rejects raw Promise workflows and imported `Effect.promise`/`Effect.tryPromise` outside exact `allowedFiles`. Recognises namespace, named, aliased and root imports, with lexical scope checks for conversion calls. An adapter allowance still requires native-first review; lint cannot determine whether every SDK has a native replacement. |
   183	
   184	The import resolver follows top-level imports and static member paths. It is
   185	not a complete scope/type analyser or arbitrary local-alias resolver. Keep
   186	shadowing prohibited/reviewed; do not claim this syntactic check proves every
   187	possible call. A rule that only matches a removed API can stay configured yet
   188	do nothing. Verify installed exports and exercise the current spelling.
   189	Do not add a Cloudflare binding allowance when the published Alchemy bridge
   190	already owns conversion. Qualify aliases, shadowed names, neighbouring paths,
   191	wildcard/parent-path rejection and accepted exact adapters with the real Oxlint
   192	command, not source-pattern assertions alone.
   193	
   194	For a project that explicitly chooses unpatched Alchemy, add the opt-in
   195	[package-policy check](../../../alchemy-iac/assets/unpatched-alchemy.ts) to its
   196	existing dependency checker. This is a manifest/lock/resolution check, not a
   197	TypeScript lint rule. Supply real parsed documents and installed manifests for
   198	every declared importing owner. Exercise active root/workspace/lock patches,
   199	mixed versions, missing resolution evidence, unrelated package patches and
   200	malformed lock data. Fresh-install, bundle and saved-state proof remain separate;
   201	follow [native migrations](../../../alchemy-iac/references/operations/native-migrations.md).
   202	
   203	Extend the existing fixture suite with invalid _and valid_ cases for imports,
   204	aliases, factory calls and configured runtime paths. Require the actual
   205	Oxlint command to examine the intended file, return a failing exit with the
   206	expected rule for a negative case, and return cleanly for the valid case.
   207	Regex-only tests do not prove that the plugin is loaded. Keep imported snapshots
   208	unchanged with their revision/hash and disposition; edit owned portable rules
   209	at their canonical owner. Document exact adapter exceptions and false positives,
   210	such as `Output.map` being mistaken for an array method.
   211	
   212	## Structural tests
   213	
   214	Add tests that inspect:
   215	
   216	- package exports;
   217	- forbidden dependency direction;
   218	- service operation error/requirement shape where TypeScript assertions are practical;
   219	- runtime file locations;
   220	- receipt Schemas;
   221	- provider client privacy;
   222	- application Layer ownership.
   223	
   224	Prefer enforcement that fails with a semantic message over a fragile snapshot.
   225	Use the existing lint, render and contract checks before adding another suite.
   226	Do not pin a file count that changes whenever a legitimate guide is added;
   227	check required owners, inventory consistency and distribution limits instead.
   228	Cached checks must include files they read outside their workspace, including
   229	shared configs, templates and copied skill assets. Re-run fresh when correcting
   230	cache inputs; a replayed passing result does not verify changed input.
   231	
   232	## Review sequence
   233	
   234	Review changed code in this order:
   235	
   236	1. external Schemas and brands;
   237	2. error vocabulary;
   238	3. service contract;
   239	4. live/test Layers;
   240	5. runtime boundary;
   241	6. concurrency/lifetime;
   242	7. observability;
   243	8. tests;
   244	9. exports and file ownership.

- Plugin 0.6.11’s `effect-policy.ts` has 13 rules, including new `static-layers` and `module-ownership` rules.
- TaxKit loads an older 11-rule copy from `.agents`. Common Practice vendors almost the same older copy; its only difference is allowing native Alchemy `Namespace.push`.
- Common Practice separately implements static Layers, private Promise adapters, SDK privacy and browser-runtime ownership in its own rule file.
- Several anti-slop files are identical between the repos. Common Practice’s retained TaxKit rules are older than TaxKit’s current implementation.
- Tool versions differ: TaxKit uses Oxlint/plugins **1.86.0**, Ultracite **7.12.2**, Effect tooling **0.48.0**; Common Practice uses **1.85.0**, **7.12.0**, **0.45.0**. Reusing rules does not require downgrading TaxKit.

| Area | Recommended source-to-target change |
|---|---|
| Portable Effect rules | Vendor the current plugin’s single `effect-policy.ts` under `tools/oxlint/vendor/strict-effect`. Enable all relevant rules across owned apps, packages, tools, configuration and tests. Remove the executable `.agents` copy and duplicate rules once equivalent behaviour is demonstrated. |
| Static Layers | Enable `strict-effect/static-layers`. Replace internal factories with static Layers whose named requirements carry checked caller settings. Native inline composition callbacks remain allowed. The rule recognises aliases, return types and common Layer-preserving operations. |
| Host/SDK ownership | Configure `strict-effect/module-ownership` for Alchemy, Cloudflare bindings, private SDKs and authored/generated content imports. It checks imports, re-exports, import types and known dynamic import addresses. TaxKit’s current host-contract rule does **not** cover Alchemy or `cloudflare:workers`. |
| Promise adapters | Use current `strict-effect/no-promise-workflow` with exact host/SDK files. Keep TaxKit’s `effect/no-bare-effect-try-promise` to require a checked error mapping. No allowance for every `*.layer.ts` or every test. Use `promiseOnlyFiles` where a host test needs only `Effect.promise`. |
| Runtime ownership | Keep one server runtime and one browser Atom runtime. Port Common Practice’s browser `Atom.runtime`/`RegistryProvider` ownership check using TaxKit’s real paths. Keep the SDK’s necessary private Promise runtime as an exact library adapter. |
| External decoding | Retain TaxKit’s `no-decoding-outside-boundaries` and `no-route-transport-restore-outside-consumers`: their lexical alias tracking and actual CLI fixtures cover useful behaviour beyond the portable rules. Keep encoding at the owning outward boundary. |
| Mutable state | Keep current portable collection rules **and** TaxKit’s lexical `no-native-collections`/`no-object-writes`. The latter follows constructor aliases and Object/Reflect writes which the portable rule does not fully cover. State belongs in Effect Ref/collections; pure folds do not need Ref. |
| Raw HTTP work | Extend raw-fetch restrictions across owned source. TaxKit currently bans bare `fetch` only in selected analytics files. Native HttpClient or an exact unavoidable host adapter should own it. |
| Package boundaries | Adapt the plugin’s manifest-derived export check to TaxKit’s actual nested workspaces. Preserve SDK packed/export/downstream checks. The current cross-package rule checks `/src` paths and `@scope/package/src`, but does not validate all exported subpaths or imports starting outside `/src`. |
| Effect diagnostics | Replace the one-file compatibility probe with strict diagnostics over actual apps, packages, tools and Alchemy roots. Preserve normal TypeScript checks. Common Practice already runs strict diagnostics on its root and packages. |

Common Practice’s apparent instrumentation rule hard-codes old services such as `Distribution` and `ManifestSync`, and recognises the literal identifier `Effect`. It does not enforce Content or TaxKit service methods. Do not copy it and claim complete coverage. [Implementation](/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/tools/oxlint/vendor/commonplace/effect-rules.js:287).
- **Configuration:** use the owning Schema through `Config.schema` for constrained settings. TaxKit’s API and Website already do this; the old HTTP config uses `Config.URL` followed by a synchronous `.make`. The scaffold’s primitive-config regex matches obsolete lowercase names and scans only one-level `package/src` folders. It misses TaxKit’s nested packages and current Config spellings. Native `Config.Boolean` remains appropriate for a plain flag; a blanket primitive ban would be wrong. [Template scan](/Users/cooper/.codex/plugins/cache/commonplace/development-workflows/0.6.11/skills/repo-structure/assets/repository/tools/oxlint/policy.test.ts.tmpl:159).
- **Absence:** portable `no-unsafe-option-unwrap` rejects `getOrThrow`, but not `getOrNull`/`getOrUndefined`. Add a focused domain rule if desired, while allowing real protocol/compiler adapters. Preserve TaxKit’s nested Option model that distinguishes a missing key from a present undefined key. Common Practice’s nullable rule merely catches `Schema.NullOr` and literal null properties; it cannot prove every domain type is non-nullable.
- **Schema-derived types:** existing unknown/type-assertion checks help, but none proves that every handwritten type reuses its owning Schema. Retain type-level checks and focused review; avoid claiming that a broad regex solves this.
- **False positives:** the current portable rule already allows functional `Output.map` and native `Namespace.push`. Do not add wide exceptions for those. `.at`, `.json` and runtime method names are matched syntactically, so unrelated methods can collide. Exceptions should name the actual file and operation.
- **Suppressions:** TaxKit’s two-pass directive check makes inline suppression of the two boundary rules fail. Keep that effective protection. It does not protect every other lint rule. A nearby `SAFETY:` comment does not permit a type assertion while the ordinary assertion ban is active.

Its base config also excludes warnings/suggestions from compiler failure. That establishes tool compatibility, not application-wide Effect correctness. [Probe configuration](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/tools/effect-language-service/tsconfig.json:9), [base settings](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/tsconfig.base.json:4), [Common Practice settings](/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/tsconfig.base.json:19).

Two genuine design choices remain:

1. **Existing public Layer factories:** HTTP exports include `createTaxKitApiClientLayer` and its deprecated alias. The new static-Layer rule permits no factory exceptions. Either retire those public helpers in a deliberate breaking package change, or explicitly allow their narrow compatibility adapter temporarily. Internal RPC, Content and Website factories can change without weakening the rule. [Public helpers](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/api/http/src/client/live.layer.ts:12).
2. **Object-only Effect inputs:** Common Practice requires every reusable `fn`/`fnUntraced` operation to take one object. That would change established TaxKit SDK methods and valid branded-value helpers. I recommend keeping existing checked signatures and applying named-object inputs only where several inputs need a meaningful combined contract.

Do not copy Common Practice’s training identifiers, training/appearance dependency rules or product-specific paths. Reuse their ownership approach for TaxKit’s calculator identities, tax packages, content and host adapters. Retain a compact actual-CLI fixture suite proving rejection **and** acceptance, including aliases, neighbouring files and nested packages. No receipt, qualification ledger or governance register is needed.

No files changed and no tests or provider calls ran.
